title: Opening
sentences: The best waste is the waste we never create.
Good morning, respected judges, teachers and dear friends. Jai Hind!
I am Avni Choudhary from Class 6, and my topic is Clean India Mission and Waste Management.
Every day, we throw away plastic, peels and paper.
But — where does all this waste go?
Let me show you how to keep our land, water and air clean.

title: Clean India Mission
sentences: The Clean India Mission, or Swachh Bharat Abhiyan, was launched on 2 October 2014 by Prime Minister Narendra Modi, on Mahatma Gandhi's birth anniversary.
Its first big goal was toilets for everyone, for our health and our water.
Cities alone built over 63 lakh home toilets.
Today, about 5.7 lakh villages are ODF Plus — free from open defecation, and managing their waste.

title: Waste management & segregation
sentences: Waste management has five main steps: separate, collect, transport, recycle or treat, and safely dispose.
The first step is the most important — segregation at source.
In my five bins, wet waste, like peels, becomes compost or biogas, and dry waste, like paper and metal, is recycled.
Mixed waste becomes garbage.
Separated waste becomes a resource.

title: Plastic & the Plastic Man
sentences: Then there is single-use plastic.
A carry bag is used for a few minutes, but it stays in nature for years and years.
But Professor Rajagopalan Vasudevan, the Plastic Man of India, showed how waste plastic can help make roads.
He got the Padma Shri in 2018.

title: The 7Rs
sentences: Not just the 3Rs — my project has 7Rs: Refuse, Reduce, Reuse — Repair, Repurpose — Recycle and Recover.
Remember my first line?
The best waste is the waste we never create.

title: Waste to energy
sentences: The last R, Recover, means getting energy back from waste.
In a biogas plant, microbes break down wet waste without oxygen and make biogas for cooking.
Leftover waste that cannot be recycled can be burnt in a closed waste-to-energy plant, with pollution control.
The heat makes steam, which turns a turbine to make electricity.
But remember — we must never burn plastic in the open.

title: Clean water & rivers
sentences: Clean water is precious.
My filter has layers, from coarse to fine: stones and gravel, charcoal, and cotton.
It comes out clearer — but clear water is not always safe to drink.
Factories need effluent treatment plants, and cities need sewage treatment plants, so dirty water is cleaned before it reaches our rivers.
Here in Gorakhpur, people cleaned Ram Ghat on the Rapti, and sent about 170 kilos of plastic and other waste for sorting and recycling.
Rivers are not dustbins.

title: Green energy & the hydrogen train
sentences: Last, a clean India also needs clean air.
Energy from the sun and the wind does not run out, and causes very little pollution.
Solar panels and windmills turn this energy into electricity.
India has crossed 300 gigawatts of clean power capacity, and aims for 500 by 2030. On 17 July 2026, India's first hydrogen train was flagged off on the Jind–Sonipat line in Haryana.
Instead of diesel smoke, it gives out mainly water vapour.

title: Our duties & conclusion
sentences: So, what can we do?
Stop littering.
Segregate waste at home and school.
Say no to single-use plastic.
Plant trees.
And my question — where does all this waste go?
If we separate it, it can come back as compost, energy and new things.
A clean India is not just a dream; it is a responsibility we share.
Thank you. Jai Hind!
